Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexusGuard Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please refrain from placing your line on hold as it may cause feedback into the conference. Today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexusGuard Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Security Officer; Rachel Kim, VP of Sales; and David Ruiz, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report another strong quarter for NexusGuard Technologies. Our results reflect the growing importance of cybersecurity in today's digital landscape and our ability to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The market reception to NexGen XDR 5.0 has been overwhelmingly positive, significantly contributing to our accelerated growth and market share gains.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. As we dive into the details of our recent product and feature launches, I'm thrilled to report that these innovations have been a key driver behind our 28% year-over-year revenue growth in the cybersecurity segment. With ransomware incidents surging 62% globally in 2023 according to Chainalysis data, and cloud-native attacks up 45% per the latest Verizon DBIR, our launches are laser-focused on addressing these pain points head-on. We've prioritized AI/ML integration, zero-trust enforcement, and autonomous response capabilities to help our customers reduce MTTR from days to minutes.

First, our flagship launch: NexGen XDR 5.0 with Autonomous Threat Hunting. Rolled out in late Q2, this extended detection and response platform unifies endpoint, network, cloud, and identity signals into a single pane of glass, leveraging our proprietary GenAI engine—built on transformer-based models trained on over 10 trillion security events. Key features include behavioral anomaly detection that flags 92% of zero-day exploits in under 60 seconds, and auto-remediation workflows that quarantine threats without human intervention. We've integrated it seamlessly with leading SIEMs like Splunk and Elastic, plus native support for Kubernetes environments to tackle container escape vulnerabilities.

The uptake has been explosive: 4,200 new subscriptions in Q3 alone, representing 35% of our total ARR bookings. Early adopters like a Fortune 100 financial services firm reduced their alert fatigue by 78%, dropping false positives from 15,000 to 3,200 per day. Financially, XDR 5.0 contributed $320 million in new ARR, with a net retention rate of 118%—customers expanding 20% on average post-deployment. Strategically, this positions us directly against CrowdStrike's Falcon and Microsoft Defender, where we've captured 12 points of market share in the EDR/XDR space per IDC's Q3 tracker, growing from 14% to 26%.

Next, ZeroTrust Edge 2.5, our SASE platform enhancement launched mid-Q3. This builds on our ZTNA core with dynamic micro-segmentation powered by eBPF for kernel-level enforcement, supporting hybrid workforces and multi-cloud setups on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. New features include frictionless identity orchestration via Okta and Ping integrations, plus ML-driven risk scoring that adapts access policies in real-time—think continuous authentication scoring user behavior against 500+ threat indicators.

Regionally, this has resonated strongly in EMEA, where GDPR and NIS2 compliance demands are accelerating zero-trust adoption. We've signed 15 major deals in the region, including a €50 million contract with a leading German automotive OEM, driving 42% YoY growth in EMEA billings. In APAC, despite geopolitical headwinds, we've seen 55% growth, fueled by Singapore's cybersecurity levy and Australia's Essential Eight framework—our Tokyo data center launch has reduced latency to under 50ms for Japanese enterprises. Overall, ZeroTrust Edge bookings hit $210 million in Q3, with 65% from net-new logos, and we've expanded our magic quadrant positioning, now challenging Zscaler's leadership in Forrester's Wave for SSE.

Finally, a game-changer for ransomware defense: RansomShield Recover, our immutable backup and AI-orchestrated rollback feature embedded across our portfolio. Using blockchain-ledgered snapshots and GenAI for forensic reconstruction, it enables point-in-time recovery with 99.999% data integrity, even post-encryption. Tested against Conti and LockBit variants, it restores systems 8x faster than traditional air-gapped backups.

This launched in early Q3 and has already protected 2.5 million endpoints. A standout case: a U.S. healthcare provider recovered from a Ryuk attack in 4 hours, avoiding a $12 million ransom—our tool auto-identified and rolled back 97% of encrypted files. Revenue impact? $145 million in upsell ARR from existing customers, with 40% adoption among our top 500 accounts. In North America, federal sector wins—including a DoD prime contractor under CMMC 2.0—have boosted our U.S. government pipeline by 60%, positioning us for the $10 billion JADC2 modernization wave.

Looking ahead, these launches underscore our 'Autonomous Security Mesh' strategy: converging AI, zero-trust, and recovery into a proactive fabric that scales with quantum threats and supply chain risks. We've invested $250 million in R&D this year, including a new quantum-resistant crypto module compliant with NIST PQC standards. Customer feedback via NPS scores at 72 reflects this—up 15 points QoQ.

Early indicators for Q4 are strong: pipeline up 32%, with 70% weighted towards these new SKUs. We're on track for 25-30% full-year growth, outpacing the 12% CAGR projected by Gartner for cybersecurity through 2027.

Our strategy is built on seven key pillars: innovative product and feature launches driving market leadership, robust channel partner performance fueling scalable growth, disciplined churn management ensuring customer stickiness, superior competitive win rates capturing share, strong net dollar retention through land-and-expand dynamics, exceptional customer feedback validating our innovations, and accelerating ARR growth across segments and regions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $450 million in the third quarter, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained healthy at 78%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $320 million. Net income was $85 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.65. We are raising our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I dive deeper into forward guidance, I'd like to highlight our channel partner performance and their contribution to revenue. NexusGuard has long prioritized a partner-first strategy in the cybersecurity landscape, competing with Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Zscaler. Our channel ecosystem—spanning VARs, MSPs, distributors like TD Synnex and Arrow Electronics, and GSIs such as Accenture and Deloitte—remains the backbone of our go-to-market.

In Q3, channel partners drove 65% of our total revenue, up from 60% in the prior-year quarter—that's $292.5 million out of $450 million, representing 35% YoY growth for the channel segment, outpacing our direct sales growth of 22% YoY. This reflects surging demand for XDR amid ransomware attacks like Change Healthcare and the shift to zero-trust with hybrid cloud. Our NexusGuard XDR, with AI-powered behavioral analytics and integrations into AWS Security Hub and Microsoft Sentinel, has excelled through channels.

Distributors contributed 42% of channel revenue at $122.7 million, up 28% YoY, strong in mid-market with Endpoint Guardian bundled. MSPs and MSSPs hit 31% or $96.1 million, +52% YoY, via MDR with API-first architecture for white-label. VARs and GSIs at 27% or $83.7 million, +22% YoY, with co-sell in financial services against supply chain risks.

Our top 20 partners grew 45% YoY, 55% of channel bookings, with recurring revenue at 82% of channel ACV from CWPP subscriptions. Regionally: North America 55% or $160.9 million +32% YoY on CISA zero-trust; EMEA 25% or $73.1 million +25% YoY on NIS2; APAC 13% or $38.2 million +68% YoY on Essential Eight; LATAM 7% or $21.2 million +18% YoY.

We've certified over 5,200 engineers via SecureChannel Academy on GenAI Threat Intelligence, co-innovation labs with AWS/Azure MSPs boosting win rates 25%, PartnerStack for deals, and Elite Tier incentives. Targeting 70% channel mix by FY2025.

Next, on churn rate and reasons for churn, which underscore our platform stickiness. We measure gross dollar churn and NRR. For Q3, gross dollar churn was 4.2% quarterly or 7.8% annualized—lowest in three years, 180 bps better YoY from 6.0%, sixth straight decline. 98% gross retention in enterprises over $1M ARR; FY22 cohort at 3.5%. Commercial 5.1%, enterprise 2.9%.

NRR at 118%, with $42 million expansions to Next-Gen SIEM and CWPP. Reasons: economic pressures 38% from budgets/tech layoffs, mitigated by flexible pricing; competitive 29% from Cortex/Singularity, countered by GenAI co-pilot; M&A 18%; technical 10%; other 5%. Regional: NA 3.8%, EMEA 5.2%, APAC 6.1%. Initiatives: ML churn prediction, ecosystem expansions, regional tailoring—expect 4.0% Q1.

On competitive win rates, a key indicator. Q3 overall 51%, up 900 bps QoQ from 42%, 1,400 bps YoY from 37%, driving $178 million new ARR from displacements, 62% of bookings. TCV $4.2M/deal.

By segment: EDR 58% displacing Falcon/Defender on fewer false positives; SASE 54% vs Zscaler; cloud 49% vs Prisma. Vs CrowdStrike 56%, Palo Alto 61%, legacy 65-68%. Regions: NA 53%, EMEA 48%, APAC 42%. Driven by $250M R&D GenAI, Microsoft co-sell, playbooks. Guide 52-54% Q4.

Net Dollar Retention—or NDR—at 118%, up 300 bps QoQ from 115%, 500 bps YoY from 113%. 11th quarter >110%. Gross retention 98.2%, expansions 20.4% from XDR/SASE. Top customers 145%, mid-market 112%. NA 122%, EMEA 116%, APAC 125%. Validated by platformization, QBRs. Guide 119-121% Q4.

Finally, ARR ended Q3 at $590 million, 11.2% QoQ from $530 million, 42.8% YoY from $413 million. New ACV $28M, expansions $19M, DBNRR 128%. Segments: Endpoint/XDR $235M +13% QoQ/48% YoY; Cloud $206M +16%/55%; Network/SASE $149M +8%/35%. Regions: NA 62% +10%/45%; EMEA +14%/52%; APAC 18% +20%/68%. Guide Q4 10-12% QoQ.

Now, over to Dr. Patel.

Dr. Lena Patel: Thank you, Mike. Our technology roadmap is focused on delivering next-generation security solutions that leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas include advancing our GenAI threat hunting and quantum-resistant capabilities.

Thank you for the handoff. Before Q&A, deeper on customer feedback on new products/features—trust is key amid AI phishing up 67% YoY and supply chain risks. NPS up 28% QoQ to 78, above Gartner 62 benchmark; CSAT 94% for launches, MTTR to <6 hours.

Apex XDR 2.0: 65% false positive cut, Fortune 500 bank: 70% alert fatigue drop, $47M ARR. QuantumShield: 91% satisfaction, EMEA telco 40% performance gain. GenAI Threat Hunter: 96% CSAT, 52% MTTR cut, healthcare flagged ShadowPad.

Regions: NA 82 NPS, APAC 75, LATAM 71 improving. Learnings: integrations addressed via toolkit, false positives via updates. $150M R&D for autonomous SOAR.

Tom Hargrove: We are committed to providing our customers with the highest level of security. We constantly monitor the threat landscape—ransomware, APTs—and adapt our posture with proactive measures like RansomShield.

Rachel Kim: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team focuses on building relationships with customers and partners, leveraging competitive wins and channel momentum.

David Ruiz: Our marketing efforts center on brand awareness and demand generation via digital, PR, events—amplifying feedback like NPS 78 and positioning us in Magic Quadrants.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Press *01 to ask a question. First question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, can you expand on the product launches and how they're impacting pipeline?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. As I detailed, NexGen XDR 5.0, ZeroTrust Edge 2.5, and RansomShield Recover have driven explosive uptake—$675M combined new/upsell ARR. Pipeline up 32%, 70% weighted to these, positioning for 25-30% FY growth amid threats.

John Doe: Follow-up: Any color on federal traction?

Alex Rivera: Strong—DoD wins under CMMC boosted gov pipeline 60%, eyeing JADC2.

Operator: Next question from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley.

Jane Smith: Great results. Mike, thoughts on churn and NDR sustainability given macro?

Mike Chen: Jane, gross churn 4.2% lowest ever, NDR 118% via 20.4% expansions. Proactive scoring, integrations offset risks—guide sub-7% annualized, NDR 119-121% Q4. Expansions cover 140% churn.

Jane Smith: And channel concentration?

Mike Chen: Top 5 at 32%, but 78% margins mitigate; Elite incentives diversify.

Operator: Next from Bob Lee with Piper Sandler.

Bob Lee: Impressive ARR QoQ. Lena, tech roadmap tie-in?

Dr. Lena Patel: Bob, ARR 11.2% QoQ to $590M aligns with AI-native roadmap—GenAI on 15T signals cuts MTTR 40%. Feedback NPS 78, CSAT 96% on Threat Hunter. Q4 MDR launch targets 20% attach.

Bob Lee: Regional APAC strength?

Dr. Lena Patel: 125% NDR, 68% YoY on DPDP/Essential Eight, localized feeds.

Operator: Next from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen: Solid wins. Tom or Rachel, competitive dynamics?

Tom Hargrove: Lisa, win rates 51% overall, 58% EDR vs Falcon—superior analytics, MITRE scores. Monitoring threats ensures posture.

Rachel Kim: Sales execution via playbooks up PoC conversion 28%; vs Palo Alto 61%.

Lisa Chen: Win rates outlook?

Rachel Kim: 52-54% Q4, platformization sustains.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
